items.title: Lou Donaldson — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: So finally, Wilbur Ware staggers in there, and Bob Reisner takes him around the corner and gives him some vitamins

ctx.x: Any bandstand memories? Anything positive you can say about the music...

Well, what happened the first night, see, he was expecting Oscar Pettiford, and they brought Mingus in there, and he didn’t like Mingus, and he played ensembles, but he never took a solo. And about the second set, I was asking Kenny Dorham, I said, “when is he going to play?” He said, “He’s not. He don’t like Mingus.” I was a low guy on the totem pole. I didn’t have much to say either. So finally, Wilbur Ware staggers in there, and Bob Reisner takes him around the corner and gives him some vitamins...and he comes…
Well, he loved Wilbur Ware, yeah.
